reason: E1 supports the concept that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves room-temperature ductility in refractory high-entropy alloys, but it does not involve NbMoTaW, Ti/Zr additions, or any irradiation testing. The remaining premises about specific element additions, irradiation tolerance mechanisms, high-temperature strength retention, and baseline irradiation resistance are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Adding Ti or Zr to NbMoTaW can induce an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix.
An inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves room-temperature ductility while maintaining high strength.
Precipitate-matrix interfaces in this microstructure enhance irradiation tolerance by promoting defect recombination and reducing blistering/amorphization.
The ductility and irradiation improvements apply up to 1600 °C and under reactor-relevant helium irradiation.
The baseline single-phase BCC NbMoTaW has poor room-temperature ductility and only computationally inferred irradiation resistance.
